title: Weak Squares and Color Complexes
summary: Holes a pawn can never cover again

steps.title: Four Pawns, One Color
steps.text:
Pawns never walk back. That single rule is what turns a square into permanent property.

Black's four center pawns stand on c6, d5, e6 and f5 — every one of them a light square, and not one able to reverse. A square that no pawn of yours can attack again is a **weak square**, or a **hole**. Look at e5. Only the d-pawn and the f-pawn ever covered it, and both have already marched past.

Pieces can watch a hole. Pawns are what hold one, and Black has none left for e5.

steps.title: Moving In
steps.text:
{{Ne5}}, and the knight is home. Black tucks the king away with {{O-O}}, which changes nothing at all about e5 — no pawn is coming to evict a piece that stands there.

That is what a hole is worth. Not a square you visit. A square you occupy, with the option of sending a second piece after the first.

One black piece still argues: the bishop on d6. It is the only black piece that touches e5, and it is the whole of Black's dark-square defense.

steps.prompt: Guard your knight with a piece as well as the pawn, choosing one that can trade off Black's only dark-square defender.
steps.hint: Your bishop on c1 has two diagonals out of the corner, and only one of them crosses a square that covers e5.

steps.title: A Whole Color, Sold
steps.text:
A new board, and the trade has already happened: Black's dark-squared bishop went for a knight, and there is no shop that sells another one.

One hole is a nuisance. A whole color is a plan. The knight on e7 stands on a dark square, which means every square it attacks is a light one. And no black pawn will ever defend g7 — the only squares one could do that from are f8 and h8, and a pawn arriving on the eighth rank stops being a pawn.

steps.title: What White Paid
steps.text:
The two white pawns on the c-file are the receipt. White took doubled pawns and a king with no comfortable home on the queenside, and bought that bishop with them. Both sides knew the terms.

Now collect. g7 is a pawn nobody defends, standing in the doorway of the home the black king still has to move into, and White's queen has a clear road toward it.

> Before you trade a bishop, count the squares it was guarding. You are selling those too, and they do not come back.

steps.prompt: Aim your queen at the kingside pawn that no black piece is left to defend.
steps.hint: Which pawn beside the black king has no defender at all now that the bishop is gone?
